label: Historicized coloniality of power as transformation of communal into lethal patriarchy
description: Engaging Quijano’s coloniality of power, Segato demonstrated that European colonization converted low-intensity Indigenous gender dualities into modern lethal patriarchy.
dialecticalTension: Adds historical-anthropological depth to decolonial gender theory.
historicalContext: University of Brasília & La guerra contra las mujeres (2003–2016).

label: Debated Oyěwùmí’s non-gender thesis to formulate Indigenous dual-gender historicity
description: Engaging Oyěwùmí’s Yorùbá findings, Segato argued that many precolonial American societies exhibited "low-intensity patriarchy" radically restructured by colonial state power.
dialecticalTension: Productive South-South debate between Yorùbá non-gender and Andean-Amazonian gender duality.

citations.author: Rita Segato
citations.work: La crítica de la colonialidad en ocho ensayos

label: Formulated the Pedagogy of Cruelty
description: Segato theorized feminicide and paramilitary terror as pedagogical rituals that train subjects in callousness to serve extractive sovereignty.
dialecticalTension: Diagnoses patriarchal violence as structural sovereign communication, not private deviance.

label: Informed Caribbean and Latin American decolonial feminist critiques of white feminism
description: Segato’s analysis of coloniality, race, and patriarchal mandates enters into ongoing dialogue with Espinosa Miñoso’s decolonial feminist school.
dialecticalTension: Links anthropological coloniality of gender with Afro-Caribbean decolonial feminism.
